crime: As a child, {WITCH_NAME} ate her meals on the stairs, one hand through the banister. Her stepfather trimmed that hand off the family photo so it would fit the frame.

In the prison, one girl sketched the courtyard from the fountain every evening, then inked the page in the library before lockup. Each time, she drew {WITCH_NAME}'s arms, hanging through the upper railing, as two sleeves. {WITCH_NAME} sat behind the railing and looked through the artist's eyes, watching her own sleeves being drawn in.
One evening the artist rubbed the sleeves out of the page. They hung over the courtyard, she said, not in it.

{WITCH_NAME} hung her empty cardigan through the bars, a pool ball in each cuff. Every night she looked through the eyes of a girl at the fountain and nudged the sleeves until they hung the way her arms did. Then, in the library, she locked her bare arms around the artist's throat until the girl lay still over the page she had inked.

In the trial court, the prisoners ruled {WITCH_NAME} out: her sleeves had been hanging through the railing while the artist died in the library. Then one prisoner pointed to the cardigan's cuffs, stretched round to the size of a pool ball. The prisoners understood. Those sleeves had hung there weighted and empty while she was in the library.
fields.epitaph: Every evening someone drew her in, and she only ever watched for the cut.
fields.epithet: The Girl at the Edge of the Picture
execution: The execution stand was a giant family picture cast in iron, with a trimming blade hinged above one edge. It chained her across that edge, her arms laid inside the picture. She looked through the spectators' eyes and saw only her sleeves inside the frame. The blade came down along the edge and through her shoulders. She slumped, still, beyond the edge, her sleeves left lying inside the iron picture.

magic.name: Borrowed Eyes
magic.text: She sees through the eyes of anyone she looks at, and can watch herself from where they stand.
